speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand, could you tell me if you experienced any specific injury or trauma recently, and is the pain localized to a particular spot on your wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

text: The pain worsening when holding your infant is a classic sign of de Quervain's tenosynovitis. Can you confirm if you feel pain specifically at the base of your thumb when you try to make a fist with your thumb tucked inside your fingers?
